title: I accidentally picked the worst kind of game for AI continuity errors
author: Plastic-Clock5067
selftext:
I made a browser mystery called Slide Fourteen with generative AI, and I accidentally chose a genre where AI continuity mistakes are especially painful.

It’s a fake university archive from 1997.

The player reads old emails, research notes, library records, personnel files, specimen records and a lot of deliberately boring little documents. The deeper part of the game is figuring out what actually happened by comparing them.

So if the AI forgets something and contradicts itself by accident... that looks exactly like a clue. lol

My workflow ended up being a bit different from what I expected.

I didn’t write a complete story and have ChatGPT fill in the prose. I gave it the world, direction and constraints, then let it generate a surprising amount of the actual material — writing, character ideas, site/code work, visuals, endings, even hidden material.

Then I became the continuity police.

I would reject things that were too generic, too obvious, wrong for 1997, out of character, or incompatible with something we had already kept.

But I didn’t automatically reject things just because I hadn’t planned them.

Sometimes the model invented a connection or motif that surprised me. I’d go back through the archive and basically try to break it. If it still fit, it could become canon.

That was probably the biggest lesson from the project for me:

AI generation wasn’t the bottleneck. Selection and consistency were.

Keeping the setting relatively small helped a lot. So did repeatedly treating old generated material as fixed source material instead of quietly regenerating history whenever a new idea appeared.

The finished game also uses external AI as part of play: the human browses the archive while their own AI acts as an Analyst for damaged/structured records, with some information split between the two.

It’s free in browser if you want to see what survived the QA:

[https://crossphase-studio.itch.io/slide-fourteen](https://crossphase-studio.itch.io/slide-fourteen)

Has anyone else hit this inversion? Once your model can generate faster than you can properly review, does QA/selection become the real bottleneck in your AI game workflow?
